Chapter 12: Spirituality and Purpose—The Zodiac as a Guide to Meaning.
When you think about it, the search for meaning is something we all wrestle with at some point in our lives. Spirituality, in whatever form it takes for you, is really about reaching out—connecting to something bigger than yourself. That might be a higher power, a deep sense of purpose, or just tuning in to the natural world around you. And here’s where astrology steps in with a fresh perspective, inviting you to see your motives as part of a much larger story.
Picture someone who feels an undeniable pull toward service, always wanting to help out in quiet, behind-the-scenes ways. If you’ve got strong Virgo or Pisces energy, you might recognize this in yourself—maybe volunteering, caregiving, or pouring your heart into creative work. On the other hand, think about someone who’s always restless, always chasing the next big thing. That drive for achievement or adventure? It’s classic Capricorn or Sagittarius—pushing you to climb new mountains, whether they’re real or just goals you set for yourself.
What’s wild is that most of us don’t even realize how much our sense of purpose is shaped by what motivates us. Take the artist who’s driven to create, just to get their emotions out. Or the teacher who lights up when guiding others. Even the activist who can’t help but fight for justice. All of them are following the unique threads of their zodiac influences, whether they know it or not.
Now, astrology isn’t about setting your future in stone. It’s more like offering hints or clues along the way. When you start to understand what really drives you, you can make choices that line up with your deepest values. So, if you’re someone who craves connection, you might seek out community. Or, if you need freedom like you need air, you’ll probably want to build a life with plenty of space to explore.
There’s a story I love about someone who spent years searching for their “calling.” They tried on different careers, different identities, always hoping something would finally click. But it wasn’t until they looked at their astrological chart—seeing how creativity, service, and independence all played a part—that they finally found a path that felt true. By honoring every side of themselves, they discovered a sense of purpose that had been there all along, just waiting for them to claim it.
What most people come to realize is that meaning isn’t a finish line; it’s an ongoing process. Your motives shift and grow as you gain experience and wisdom. Astrology can give you a map, but remember—the journey itself is yours, and it’s completely unique.
